transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Alex Morgan, Maya Patel - Redwood; Tom Reyes, Priya Shah, Evan Li, Sara Gomez - NexaAnalytics

Summary: quick perf/cost deep dive focusing on embeddings + reranking pipeline. referenced internal bench sheet (link: drive.re/bench-embed-1120) and security docs.

Transcript: 
00:00 Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, Alex from Redwood and Maya is our SE, and you are?
00:08 Tom (Customer): Tom Reyes, CTO at NexaAnalytics. hey, yea thanks. our main ask today is to understand cost and latency tradeoffs for our rerank workflow — we have 150 qps peak and 99p latency target of 100ms for rerank stage.
00:20 Maya (SE): great, and to confirm, rerank stage is embedding-based: candidate generation offline, then online embeddings + dot-product rerank?
00:28 Priya (ML): yes, we do candidate generation in our service and call Redwood for embedding and rerank scoring. current embeddings are 768 dims, stored in Faiss. quality is OK but cost is creeping.
00:40 Maya: ok good. a few things we'll cover: empirical perf by vector dims, batching behavior at different QPS, impact of KV cache for stateful models, and quantization options to trade mem/latency vs quality. also VPC/on-prem implications for throughput.
00:52 Evan (Infra): quick note: we need VPC peering and also an option to run on-prem for PCI-scoped jobs.
01:00 Alex: noted. quick baseline: in our internal bench with a 80GB A100 class node, generating a 768-d embedding with our open model (opt-embedding-v2) we see median latency ~6-9ms and p99 around 25-40ms when batching aggressively — those numbers vary a lot with batch size and concurrency.
01:20 Priya: 6-9ms seems optimistic; are you including serialization + network?
01:24 Maya: good call — our bench numbers include just model inference. for end-to-end add 2-6ms depending on hosted vs dedicated and network hop. for hosted in same region add ~3ms typical.
01:35 Tom: and how does dimension scale? 1024 vs 768 vs 512?
01:39 Maya: dimension effect is roughly linear with vector size for compute-bound parts. in our tests: 512 ~ 4-6ms, 768 ~ 6-9ms, 1024 ~ 9-14ms per embedding on a mid-size GPU; memory footprint goes up which affects batching. so for 150 qps you need to size batch windows carefully.
02:00 Priya: but our rerank step scores ~10 candidates per query — so that's 150*10=1500 embeddings/sec. is that right?
02:07 Alex: depends: if you generate embeddings server-side per candidate, yes. but common pattern is to precompute candidate embeddings and only compute query embedding online then do vector dot-products, cheaper. clarify: are you computing embeddings for document candidates at request time?
02:18 Priya: currently yes for some dynamic content; we want to move more to precompute but not all. dynamic subset maybe 2 per query.
02:25 Maya: ok that changes numbers — compute load is lower. for mixed workloads we recommend hybrid: precompute static set, online compute for dynamic docs. importantly, KV cache helps when you have repeated prefixes or repeated identical inputs — for rerank it's less helpful unless you cache the query embedding or candidate embeddings on the Redwood side.
02:42 Evan: can KV cache store embeddings or only model KV caches?
02:46 Maya: KV cache here refers to model autoregressive KV caching. for embeddings it's not applicable the same way. but we have a storage cache layer (prefix / embedding cache) that can cache computed embeddings per doc id for X minutes. configuring TTLs reduces duplicate compute and can massively lower cost.
03:05 Tom: let's talk batching — we see spikes. how do batching windows impact latency tail?
03:10 Maya: batching reduces amortized compute per request but adds queueing delay. small batches (1-8) give low tail at expense of lower throughput efficiency. medium batches (16-64) are sweet spot for GPU throughput but you must cap queueing time to keep p99 under SLO. e.g., at 150 qps with 10 candidates and online embedding for 2 docs: if you set batch max wait 10ms and concurrency 8 you can keep median low and p99 near 80-120ms depending on dims.
03:38 Priya: these numbers assume GPU runs continuous. what about Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private?
03:43 Alex: Dedicated gives you predictable capacity with reserved slots and less noisy neighbors; hosted is multi-tenant and can have slightly higher variance but lower management overhead; private/on-prem gives full control but requires sizing infra and we can provide a packaging with optimized kernels. For your PCI jobs you might want private for full data residency.
03:58 Evan: on-prem performance parity? we saw other vendors lose 15% perf on our infra due to kernel mismatch.
04:03 Maya: we do an install-time kernel/autotune pass; we profile ops and choose kernels. on-prem can match or exceed cloud perf if nodes are configured correctly (CUDA, cuBLAS, AMX-like libs). we will run a calibration step.
04:20 Tom: quantization — how much can we push? INT8 for embeddings?
04:24 Maya: INT8 (post-training quant) can reduce memory and improve throughput but may slightly reduce embedding quality. our quant profiles: FP16 baseline, FP16+weight-quant = small win, INT8 gives 2-3x memory saving and up to 1.5-2x throughput improvement for large batch sizes. quality drop depends on model and task — for semantic similarity tests we saw ~0.5-1.5% AUC drop for INT8 on one model, larger on others. recommend validating on your eval set.
04:52 Priya: ok, we care a lot about quality — a 1% AUC hit is concerning. are there hybrid options?
04:57 Maya: yes mixed precision and selective quantization: keep encoder layers in FP16 and quantize only matmuls or lower-importance layers, or use 8-bit for keys/values only. also you can quantize document embeddings offline (where slight drift is tolerable) and keep query embeddings high precision if that helps.
05:15 Alex: important note on rerank latency: vector search cost (Faiss/Annoy) is separate; if you offload search to a vector DB you need to account for network and indexing latency. we recommend benchmarking end-to-end. we usually see vector DB p99 of 10-50ms depending on index and sharding.
05:32 Tom: we use Faiss on-prem with IVF-PQ; p99 can spike to 200ms during reindexing.
05:37 Maya: that explains some spikes. you can mitigate with background reindexing windows, warm replicas, and keeping hot shards in memory. also, Redwood can do rerank scoring inside the same runtime to reduce cross-service hops if you want a single-step call (embedding+score).
05:55 Priya: if we did embedding + score in Redwood, what are the cost implications vs just embedding?
06:00 Alex: slightly higher per-request compute but you reduce network and DB costs. pricing wise, embedding+rerank call priced at X shape (we'll share exact number in spreadsheet). for throughput it's more efficient because we avoid an extra RPC per candidate.
06:12 Evan: security: for private data we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. is that supported on Dedicated?
06:17 Maya: yes Dedicated and Private support KMS integration and enterprise audit logs; Hosted supports customer-managed keys for some tiers. we will send SOC2 + architecture docs.
06:27 Tom: good. can we run a small bench next week? 1k sample queries, synthetic load to 200 qps to test tail?
06:33 Alex: yes, send samples and desired SLOs. we'll run on a Dedicated-like instance (A100_xx) and produce latency and cost per 1M requests numbers for dims 512/768/1024 and quant profiles FP16/INT8.
06:46 Maya: i'll include batch size sweeps (1,8,32,128) and concurrency settings plus cache-on vs cache-off runs. will annotate results with warm vs cold caches.
06:55 Priya: please show per-request cost and per-embedding FLOP estimate, or at least approximate GPU-seconds used, that helps procurement.
07:03 Alex: noted. also we'll include suggested autoscale policy: keep a small steady pool for low latency and burst to preemptive nodes when queue builds.
07:12 Tom: what about A/B on dims? can we run trial with 512 vs 768 to see quality delta?
07:16 Maya: absolutely — we'll run the same 1k queries and compute NDCG/AUC differences and include regression alerts configs.
07:23 Sara (Product): on rollout we're concerned about regressions. what does Redwood provide for evals?
07:27 Alex: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and eval suites; we can host the eval and alert when regressions exceed thresholds.
07:34 Evan: any gotchas for VPC peering latency?
07:37 Maya: minimal — cross-VPC traffic adds a few ms; the major factor is network path and NAT. for strict 10ms SLOs you want colocated infra.
07:45 Tom: ok sounds good. can you also provide rough cost delta between using larger dims vs more QC on same dims?
07:50 Alex: we'll include a delta table: cost per 1M requests, cost per GB of stored embeddings, and CPU/GPU-s cost for re-ranking per QPS for each dim/quant. expect ~1.4x cost moving from 512->768 and ~1.7x to 1024 on compute side before storage costs. quantization can cut compute cost by ~20-50% depending on profile.
08:10 Priya: final question: how do you handle cold cache warm-up for rerank? we saw 2-3x tail increase on monday mornings.
08:16 Maya: recommendation: keep hot subset of embeddings in memory and run scheduled warmers for nightly cold items; also incremental cache TTL and LRU eviction tuned to access pattern. instrument cache hit rates in Console.
08:28 Alex: ok i'm going to recap next steps — we'll share bench spreadsheet, pricing deltas, and schedule infra call. Nexa to send sample queries and SLOs.
08:36 Tom: thanks all, that covers it.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts: speaker overlaps, minor misnaming (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as "Redwood dedicate"), and punctuation inconsistencies.
